nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number. If $G$ is a $k$-degenerate simple graph on a finite vertex set, then the chromatic number of $G$ is at most $k + 1$.
nodes.title: Chromatic number of a degenerate graph

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number. Every $k$-degenerate simple graph on a finite vertex set is $(k + 1)$-colorable.
nodes.title: $k$-degenerate graphs are $(k + 1)$-colorable

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$, let $s \subseteq V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. If $G$ is $k$-degenerate on $s$, then there is a map $f : V \to \{0, 1, \dots, k\}$ such that $f(a) \ne f(b)$ for all adjacent vertices $a, b \in s$.
nodes.title: Coloring a $k$-degenerate vertex set with $k + 1$ colors

nodes.summary: If $G$ is a $k$-degenerate simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$, then $G$ has a degeneracy ordering with bound $k$: an injective map $e : V \to \mathbb{N}$ such that every vertex $v$ has at most $k$ neighbors $w$ with $e(v) < e(w)$.
nodes.title: Degenerate graphs have degeneracy orderings

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $s \subseteq V$. If $G$ is $k$-degenerate on $s$, then there is a map $e : V \to \mathbb{N}$, injective on $s$, such that every $v \in s$ has at most $k$ neighbors $w \in s$ with $e(v) < e(w)$.
nodes.title: Degeneracy orderings of a vertex set

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $s \subseteq V$ be nonempty. If $G$ is $k$-degenerate on $s$, then some vertex $v \in s$ has at most $k$ neighbors in $s$.
nodes.title: A degenerate vertex set has a vertex of small degree

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. A map $e : V \to \mathbb{N}$ is a degeneracy ordering of $G$ with bound $k$ if $e$ is injective and every vertex $v$ has at most $k$ neighbors $w$ with $e(v) < e(w)$.
nodes.title: Degeneracy ordering

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, the edgeless graph on a finite vertex set is $k$-degenerate.
nodes.title: The edgeless graph is degenerate

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex type $V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. If $G$ is $k$-degenerate, then $G$ is $k$-degenerate on every subset $U \subseteq V$.
nodes.title: A degenerate graph is degenerate on every vertex set

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex type $V$, let $U \subseteq V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. Then $G$ is $k$-degenerate on $U$ if every nonempty subset $W \subseteq U$ contains a vertex $v$ with at most $k$ neighbors in $W$.
nodes.title: Degeneracy on a vertex set

nodes.summary: A simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex type $V$ is $k$-degenerate, for a natural number $k$, if it is $k$-degenerate on the full vertex set $V$: every nonempty set $W$ of vertices contains a vertex with at most $k$ neighbors in $W$.
nodes.title: Degenerate graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set. If $G$ is $k$-degenerate and $k \le l$, then $G$ is $l$-degenerate.
nodes.title: Degeneracy is monotone in the bound

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex type $V$, let $U \subseteq V$, and let $k \le l$ be natural numbers. If $G$ is $k$-degenerate on $U$, then $G$ is $l$-degenerate on $U$.
nodes.title: Degeneracy on a vertex set is monotone in the degree bound

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set. If every vertex of $G$ has degree at most $k$, then $G$ is $k$-degenerate.
nodes.title: Bounded maximum degree implies degeneracy

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex type $V$, let $T \subseteq U \subseteq V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. If $G$ is $k$-degenerate on $U$, then $G$ is $k$-degenerate on $T$.
nodes.title: Degeneracy on a vertex set passes to subsets

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
